title: Convo Workbench: exploratory scratchpad
content:
Context
----
Quick personal brain dump for a small product experiment: "Convo Workbench" — an interactive playground inside the Console that helps developers iterate on chat + retrieval flows. Goal is to shrink iteration time when exploring prompt templates, retrieval strategies, and model variants.

Why this?
- Teams are spending a lot of time switching between local notebooks, the Hosted API, and ad-hoc infra to test retrieval + prompt combos.
- We can own a lightweight in-console experience that wires up: model selection, retrieval config, prompt templating, and a side-by-side diff view for outputs.
- Helps sales/SEs demo quickly and helps small teams validate before Dedicated/Private commitments.

High level goals
- Make it trivial to try different model + retrieval + prompt combos in < 2 minutes.
- Surface token cost estimates and latency for each run.
- Save experiments as named presets that can be promoted to routes or test harnesses.

Non-goals (for MVP)
- Not a full-blown evaluation suite (no massive batch evals).
- Not replacing Optimize (we'll surface suggestions but not automate quantization tuning).

Primary personas
- Product engineers + ML engineers wanting to prototype chat experiences.
- Solutions engineers demonstrating product fit.

Core flows / UI sketches
1) Quick Start panel (left): select dataset (upload or select embeddings index), choose model variant (gpt-style or open-model), toggle retrieval on/off, set temperature/topk, set top_p, choose chunking strategy.
2) Prompt composer (center): editable template with placeholders, variables pane, simple handlebars-like syntax, ability to inject context blocks from retrieved docs.
3) Run & Results (right): streaming output, token usage breakdown, latency, a small diff toggle to compare to previous run.
4) Presets bar (top): Save current config as preset, label it, add notes. Promote preset to route (creates route draft linked to Dashboard).

User stories (MVP)
- As an engineer, I want to swap the retrieval index and see how the model answers change, so I can pick the best KB.
- As an SE, I want to demo a canned preset in 3 clicks on a call.
- As a PM, I want to record an experiment run and annotate it with notes and expected acceptance criteria.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- R1: Users can select a model and run a prompt with/without retrieval in the Console.
- R2: Each run shows token usage and latency, and a per-run cost estimate.
- R3: Users can save and list presets (title + description + config).
- R4: Preset promotion creates a draft route with same model + config (no automatic deploy).

Metrics to track
- Time from open workbench -> first successful run (goal < 2 min).
- Preset creation rate (as proxy for value).
- Conversion of preset -> route (indicative of productionization).
- Average tokens per run and average latency.

Implementation notes (tech)
- Hook into existing Hosted API endpoints for model calls. Reuse existing cost calculator in Console.
- Retrieval: allow plugging existing Redwood indices (RDW indices) or upload CSV for local ephemeral index (use embedding endpoint + in-memory ANN for MVP).
- Storage: presets saved to user namespace in Console backend; small metadata (json) stored in Config service.
- Security: uploaded datasets ephemeral and per-user by default; option to persist under project for team use.

Open questions / risks
- Embedding compute cost for ephemeral indices — do we pre-warm or charge user? billing UX needed.
- If retrieval returns PII, need clear warning & retention policy. Coordinate with Security/Compliance.
- Scaling: streaming multiple concurrent runs in Console might stress routing—limit concurrent runs per user/account for MVP.

Experiment plan (4 weeks)
W1: Prototype UI mockups + backend wireframe (Arjun)
W2: Minimal embedding upload + ephemeral ANN lookup + model call plumbing (Sofia)
W3: Preset save/promotion + cost/latency display + basic telemetry
W4: Internal dogfood + SE demo + collect feedback -> decide go/no-go

Next steps (todo)
- Pair with Arjun on basic mockups (today)
- Slack #product-hosted-api: post concept + recruit 2 SEs for early testing
- Create JIRA-CONV-842 epic and link this doc (done?)

Notes to self
- Keep default generative model low-temp and surface an example prompt set (FAQ style) so SEs can demo retrieving docs + citations.
- Consider small 'compare' panel that runs two configs in parallel to highlight differences. Could be useful for A/B of reranker or different chunk sizes.

Rough mock of workbench layout (ASCII):
[ Dataset | Model ]  [ Prompt composer ]  [ Results (stream) ]
[ Presets: example-1 | faq-demo | se-demo ]

Links referenced
- CONFLUENCE: https://confluence.redwood/CONVOWB-ideas
- JIRA: JIRA-CONV-842 (proto-ui epic)
- GitHub: github.com/redwood-inference/convo-workbench/tree/proto-ui

Last thought: make sure the 'promote to route' flow creates a clear audit trail: who promoted, when, and a snapshot of the config. Might matter for Dedicated/Private customers.

-- maya
